Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Grounding validation & ranking approach (Skyline Health pilot)

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on the technical discussion so we can align on a short validation plan: 

• Objective: confirm retrieval+reranker combination that keeps hallucination below your tolerance threshold (Factuality error rate <= 2% on the clinical QA probe) while meeting 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for query path.
• Priority metrics to validate: grounding precision@1/3, answer-level factuality, reranker calibration (confidence vs accuracy), end-to-end 95p latency, tokens/response cost.

Immediate asks / next steps we suggested: 
1) We’ll drop a small probe (attached) with 120 representative queries across clinical notes, billing, and policy snippets. We recommend running the probe with your default embeddings + BM25 baseline so we can compare.
2) Proposed retriever configs: add exact-match filter on patient-ID fields, chunk-size 800 tokens, recall k candidates = 50 for initial experiments (see proposed_retriever_config.yaml attached).
3) Reranker options to test: (A) Redwood lightweight cross-encoder quantized model (recommended for latency), (B) Larger cross-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning (higher quality but higher cost). We noted tradeoffs on the call — we put a recommended ordering in the attached doc.
4) Prompt sets: starting prompt set and negative examples included in prompt-sets-skyline-v1.jsonl; please run the probe first and return results, then we’ll propose a tuned prompt + reranker threshold to meet your factuality target.

Attachments: skyline_rag_probe.csv (120 queries), proposed_retriever_config.yaml, prompt-sets-skyline-v1.jsonl

Questions for you:
• Can your team drop the probe run by EOD Wednesday (23 Jun)?
• Is there any PII-obfuscation requirement for the probe outputs we should follow when you share logs?

I’ll follow up with a lightweight runbook and the HubSpot link so we can track progress in the deal. Thanks — Hannah

--

Thanks Hannah — that recap is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) We can run the probe but need to confirm masking for PHI. We can return masked outputs where any 6+ digit numeric sequences and names are redacted. Is that OK for your analysis?
2) On reranker options: our infra team prefers option A (low-latency) for initial live tests. If option B shows a clear factuality uplift in the probe, we can evaluate cost/throughput tradeoffs.
3) Who should we send the probe results to? I suggest mlops@skylinehealth.com but copy your team as well.

We’ll aim to run the probe by EOD Wed (23 Jun) if procurement sign-off doesn’t block it. I’ll keep you posted.

— Alex

Alex — perfect, masking sounds fine and we’ll use masked probe outputs for analysis. A couple additional specifics to make the run actionable: 

Run instructions (minimal):
• Use the attached CSV as-is; remove any rows where you cannot reasonably mask content.
• Run retrieval with two configs: (1) your current embeddings + BM25 baseline (k=50) and (2) Redwood suggested retriever (chunk=800, k=50, patient-ID filter).
• For reranker, score the same candidate set with: lightweight cross-encoder (option A) and the larger reranker (option B) if available. Return top-5 candidates and the reranker score for the chosen top answer.
• Output columns we need: query_id, query_text_masked, top_answer_text_masked, reranker_score, candidate_ids, latency_ms, config_tag.

We’ll produce a short analysis template once we get results but the quick checks we’ll run: grounding precision@1/3, factuality-sample (10 random queries human-verified), and reranker score calibration plot.

I’m attaching a small local script snippet and the prompt set used for the initial generation to make it easier to reproduce. Please send results to mlops@skylinehealth.com and copy me + Karthik. If procurement slows you down, share a redacted sample and we’ll run a partial analysis to unblock the next steps.

Thanks — Hannah

Attachments referenced inline: skyline_rag_probe.csv (same as before), prompt-sets-skyline-v1.jsonl

Quick update: procurement approved the probe run on a redacted basis. We ran both configs this morning and attaching the results (redacted sample) for your initial analysis. High-level observations from our side: 
• Baseline (BM25 + embeddings) yields stronger recall for policy docs; Redwood retriever had slightly better context chunking for longer clinical notes.
• Latency numbers look good for option A reranker; option B not run due to cost caps on the trial.
• We noticed a cluster of false positives where candidate selection included meeting notes with boilerplate templates — looks like we should add doc-type filtering on the retriever side.

Attachment: skyline_rag_results_redacted_sample.csv (sent to mlops@skylinehealth.com). Please confirm next steps and whether Redwood can push a recommended reranker threshold and the candidate-filter addition in a short config diff.

Thanks — Alex
